question.text: A segregated portfolio (side pocket) in a mutual fund is created when:

answer.text: The scheme's AUM crosses a threshold mandating portfolio bifurcation
A credit event occurs, such as a downgrade of a holding below investment grade
The fund manager wants to concentrate bets on high-conviction stocks
An investor requests separate treatment of specific holdings

explanation.text: The Logic: A segregated portfolio is created when a credit event occurs -- specifically when a debt holding is downgraded below investment grade. The affected security is separated from the main portfolio to protect existing investors from forced liquidation at distressed prices. The Trap: Side pockets are not discretionary. They are triggered by credit events and require trustee approval. The fund manager cannot create one just for portfolio strategy purposes. Cross-Exam Context: Segregated portfolios were introduced after the credit crisis involving IL&FS and other debt defaults. NISM Series II-B and V-A both cover this protective mechanism.
